subject: Follow-up: Cost breakdown & batching assumptions for ClearSight POC
messages:
From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@clearsight.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-08T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + cost assumptions from today's call

Thanks again for the time today, Samir — good conversation. Below is a short written recap so we have the same assumptions before I put together the formal estimate and spreadsheet (attached). Please correct anything that's off.

1) Business context
- Use case: interactive analytics assistant embedded in ClearSight's dashboard (real-time Q&A, chart generation).
- Priority: responsiveness for analyst workflows (95th %-ile latency target ~300ms; acceptable up to 500ms for heavy ops).

2) Volume & budget (your confirmation needed)
- Expected steady-state token consumption: 50M–75M tokens / month (you mentioned average daily active analysts ~120 during business hours).
- Target budget: you said the team is aiming for roughly $10k–$20k / month initially and want to benchmark a target $/1M tokens figure for procurement.
- Target unit price you indicated in the call to test vs internal target: $/1M tokens in the ~$200–$300 range.

3) Technical assumptions we used for the initial estimate
- Average request payload (prompt + completion): ~320 tokens (prompt ~120 / completion ~200).
- Continuous batching expected (steady stream of small inference requests that can be combined): average batch size 6–9 tokens per micro-batch, effective batching gain ~15–25% depending on concurrency.
- KV/prefix cache reuse: moderate (we assumed ~55–65% reuse for repeated analytic prefixes), which reduces tokens actually served by the model in some flows.
- Typical concurrency window during business hours: 12–24 concurrent inference workers (burst to 40 for peak reports).

4) What I'll deliver next
- A short cost worksheet (PDF/Excel) showing: nominal cost at several $/1M token tiers, the modeled improvement from continuous batching and cache reuse, and a suggested POC configuration (hosted vs. dedicated).
- Suggested SLOs and a canary rollout plan for the POC.

Next step: if the volume and budget ranges above look correct, I'll send a one-page cost estimate + attachment today and flag any assumptions that materially change price. Also copying Marissa (sales ops) to start procurement checklist if you want to move quickly.

Thanks — talk soon.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks, Sergio — this is exactly the kind of short recap we want. A couple of quick clarifications before you lock numbers: 

- Volume: we should plan for an upper-bound scenario of 70–75M tokens/mo for the POC to be safe. Day-of-week spikes are real; weekday business hours look heavier.
- Target $/1M tokens: leadership is pushing for a target at or below $250 / 1M. If you can model 250 as a baseline and show delta to 200/300 that's helpful.
- Batching: can you show us both a steady (continuous) batching case and a spiky case where batching gains are lower (~5–8%)? Our infra team is worried that allowed concurrency will be limited in our embed.

If you can include an example monthly cost line for 70M tokens at $250/1M (and the same line with 15–20% batching uplift), that'll let procurement see if it fits our budget.

Also adding Megan (procurement) to start the paperwork — Megan, happy to connect separately for PO/contract questions.

—Samir

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@clearsight.ai>, Megan Li <megan.li@clearsight.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-08T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + cost assumptions from today's call — estimate attached

Great questions — attached is the worksheet (redwood-cost-estimate-v1.xlsx). Key lines pulled out below so you can review quickly. Numbers assume the hosted Redwood API with the model we discussed; Dedicated pricing / committed capacity would change unit economics further.

Assumptions used for the table below:
- Baseline avg tokens/request: 320 tokens.
- Monthly volume scenario used: 70,000,000 tokens.
- Baseline price tiers modeled: $300 / 1M, $250 / 1M, $200 / 1M.
- Continuous batching improvement: modeled at 18% (conservative midpoint between 15–25%).
- Spiky workload (limited batching): modeled at 7% improvement.
- Overhead & fees (network, storage for KV cache, telemetry): included as a flat add-on of $350 / month in the worksheet.

Quick math (70M tokens):
- At $300 / 1M: nominal = 70 * $300 = $21,000 / month
- At $250 / 1M: nominal = 70 * $250 = $17,500 / month
- At $200 / 1M: nominal = 70 * $200 = $14,000 / month

With continuous batching (18% effective token reduction):
- 70M effective tokens -> ~57.4M billed tokens
- At $250 / 1M -> 57.4 * $250 = $14,350 (+$350 overhead) = ~$14.7k / month

With spiky limited batching (7% reduction):
- 70M -> ~65.1M billed tokens
- At $250 / 1M -> 65.1 * $250 = $16,275 (+$350) = ~$16.6k / month

Notes about the batching & concurrency assumptions:
- "Continuous batching" here assumes a relatively steady stream of small requests during business hours; Redwood's runtime uses continuous micro-batching and KV prefix caching to reduce per-token compute when similar prefixes are common (your analytics prompts/filters make this scenario likely).
- If requests are highly bursty and isolated (large gaps between user requests), batching gains evaporate; hence the separate spiky scenario.
- Concurrency: these numbers assume the ability to support 12–24 concurrent in-flight requests with background queuing for short windows; if ClearSight limits concurrency (e.g., to <8), batching benefits will be lower and latency may improve but cost per token increases.
- Dedicated/Committed capacity: with a committed pool we can price below the hosted tiers shown; I put a sample dedicated scenario on the 2nd worksheet (savings range ~10–30% depending on commit).

Action items
1) Samir/Megan: confirm 70M tokens as the POC upper-bound and whether you want the POC to be hosted or if you want a dedicated quote.
2) Marissa: if we move to procurement, can you start the PO template and flag any required legal terms for a short POC (30 days)? I've attached a PO template for ClearSight to review.
3) Samir: confirm whether we should model a 2-week ramp vs immediate steady-state — this impacts the first-month estimate.

I'll leave the detailed row-by-row math in the spreadsheet and can turn it into a short one-pager if procurement prefers that.

Thanks — Sergio
Attachment: redwood-cost-estimate-v1.xlsx
